backbone: Weight-by-weight dimension squeeze: a char-2 pentagon degeneration bounds dim W_n, holonomy constructs odd-weight generators with nonzero x^{n-1}y coefficient, and induction yields freeness.
quote: Sections~\ref{sec:category} and~\ref{sec:holonomy} construct the odd-weight values. Section~\ref{sec:induction} completes the induction.

backbone: Sieve reduces density to a large-prime tail estimate, proved by determinant-method counting with adaptive auxiliary primes, weighted Hilbert bounds and low-degree surface/curve geometry.
quote: The density argument first holds the finite-prime cutoff fixed while $X$ tends to infinity, and then lets the cutoff tend to infinity.

backbone: Reduce Hodge classes on CM abelian varieties to algebraicity of four-factor switch lines, then realize those via a surface period criterion using theta forms on ball quotients.
quote: Section~\ref{sec:tensors} then assembles arbitrary balanced tensors from these relations: two-row switches connect lists with the same sum, and algebraic polarization pairings contract their intermediate factors.

backbone: Show both coefficient maps surjective with equal kernels: stable-pair tests give a kernel inclusion, a multipartition filtration gives a Betti-number bound, and torus-fixed and cocharacter-fixed schemes are identified.
quote: Its two main comparisons have different purposes: a calculation for the full topological torus identifies the cohomology algebra, while a separate argument identifies that torus-fixed scheme with the fixed scheme of the stability cocharacter.

backbone: Assume the Albanese fibre-group image N is infinite; a minimal base orbifold gives, in linear and nonlinear branches, positivity that descends to a Bogomolov sheaf contradicting specialness.
quote: Assuming \(N\) infinite, consider fibrations of Albanese fibres on all finite covers for which the quotient by the fibre-group image is still infinite.

backbone: Uniformize finite approximations to circle domains, pass to normalized limits, and use transboundary extremal-length barriers and fused path laws to exclude noncircular limiting components.
quote: The additional tasks here are to fuse the countable tests into one law controlling all boundary components, to preserve compatibility as tests are appended, and to exclude all possible noncircular limiting components.

backbone: Reduce the uniform L2 bound to restricted band estimates, then prove those by time-frequency tile/forest decompositions with an iterated angular phase gain from a sharp finite Fourier inequality.
quote: The proof of \Cref{thm:band-restricted} will be completed after the packet estimates and their iteration have been established. The next results show, without using that theorem as a premise elsewhere in its proof, that it implies \Cref{thm:main}.

backbone: Exhibit a determinantal hyperbolic polynomial p_Q; assuming a semidefinite lift, a positive Hankel moment functional from a certified seed matrix yields a local order-four violation.
quote: We construct a rank-twenty positive semidefinite Hankel matrix whose kernel has strong multiplication properties.

backbone: For every detecting tensor character, separation degenerations give inequalities on polynomial-multiplication profiles; their discrete growth forces character parameter t<=3/4, hence omega<=9/4.
quote: The present proof combines explicit tensor degenerations with the spectral viewpoint. It derives inequalities for character values on polynomial multiplication, then uses their discrete growth to bound the values on matrix multiplication.

backbone: Prove a local entropy-production (joining) inequality via an explicit optimizer and capacities, lift it by induction on cube dimension, and integrate along the noise semigroup.
quote: The proof combines an explicit three-point optimizer for the local joining problem, two entropy capacities, and a common-output thinning inequality, followed by dimension induction and integration along the noise semigroup.

backbone: Recursively construct nested Boolean predicates on a labelled tournament, bound sensitivity by recurrences and exhibit disjoint sensitive blocks at zero; composition amplifies to a power separation.
quote: We recursively construct nested families of Boolean predicates: their accepting sets decrease as the predicate index increases.

backbone: Build the diffeomorphism as a smooth limit of stages, each perturbation letting Koopman Laurent polynomials of f approximate a further test function, so iterates of f span L2_0.

backbone: Take rank-one projectors in R^4; a hypothetical 10-cover yields an admissible map RP^3 to a simplex whose degree and support complex force a cycle structure excluded by label case analysis.
quote: The compact set of rank-one orthogonal projectors on ℝ4, with the Frobenius metric, cannot be covered by ten sets of strictly smaller diameter.

backbone: Identify each elementary coefficient with a positive quantum-torus/scattering-diagram object via positive reordering and wall transport, then realize identities by bijections giving an explicit permutation witness.
quote: It first identifies each relevant elementary coefficient with a positive algebraic object. It then realizes the algebraic identities by finite bijections between ordered collections of independent sets.

backbone: Strong induction on n with a multiscale charging scheme: choose an expanding layer whose savings pay for decomposition work, recursing on smaller quotient graphs with a phi(n) slack.
quote: The additional mechanism is an induction that saves vertices across different scales while reserving enough edges to lift cycles from the smaller graphs.

backbone: Construct length algebras with vanishing positive Koszul lengths, then compare ordinary and normalized Euler evaluations via supported descent and norm comparison to express chi as a positive length.
quote: The two evaluations recover the factor $r$ differently: the ordinary one uses the alternating rank of a resolution of $T$, while the normalized one uses the vanishing of positive Tor lengths.

backbone: Induction on m in the cyclic staircase module: dominated shapes directly, then band quotients, width-two band detection and horizontal-strip Pieri reduction reach every partition.
quote: This is why both parts of the induction track generators instead of using ambient tensor-product support alone.

backbone: Method of moments: hierarchical Gaussian calculus and size comparisons give convergence of all rescaled moments with exponential moment bounds, identifying a unique nondegenerate limit law.
quote: It is the unique probability measure with the moments specified in Proposition~\ref{def:law} below.

backbone: A posterior-law class with a preserved degree-six polynomial constraint is closed under channel steps and products; cubic moment saving makes E A decay by depth recursion, using certified polynomial inequalities.
quote: We construct a degree-six polynomial $H$ for which the additional constraint $\E H(p)\geq0$ is preserved by both channel steps and the combination of observations.

backbone: Represent any automorphism by a Borel map (Slaman-Woodin), recover t from four values on a comeager set, and use category cone avoidance to get pi^{-1}(a) <= a and conversely.
quote: Since recovery holds on a comeager set, Lemma~\ref{lem:avoidance} removes the auxiliary degrees and yields $\pi^{-1}(\mathbf a)\leT\mathbf a$ for every degree $\mathbf a$.

backbone: Construct polygon-algebra groups A_m; prove simplicity, amenability via random polygonal partitions, finitely generated Schur multiplier via homological stability, and build a finitely presented central cover.
quote: We construct an infinite finitely presented simple amenable group, giving a positive answer to the finite-presentation existence question for simple amenable groups.

backbone: Bound collar mutual information via spectral-gap norm comparisons on replica operators (bootstrapping a box exponent), then entropy chain rules over ordered region families give the area law.
quote: If each region shares little information with the complement of $A$ together with the earlier regions of its own family, two applications of the entropy chain rule cancel all individual region entropies.

backbone: A transfer lemma converts conditioning bounds on tested coordinate sets into exponential threshold bounds; combined with Song's conditioning estimate it yields the universal rate.
quote: We obtain this theorem by combining a transfer from conditioning bounds to threshold bounds with Song's conditioning estimate~\cite[Lemma~4.4]{song2026}.

backbone: Prove finite-factor conjugacy (commutator amplification plus boundary averaging), reduce infinite factors via modular alignment and crossed products, then assemble through centers and arbitrary Hilbert spaces.
quote: \Cref{fig:proof} displays how the finite-factor result enters both the finite and infinite cases and how they meet in the final reductions.

backbone: Classification by existence and uniqueness: transport the trace cone, build sequence models with corrected trace formulas, prove norm uniqueness, and conclude by approximate intertwining.
quote: The existence, uniqueness, and approximate-intertwining organization of those classification arguments also provides the broad method used here, with new local estimates needed for arbitrary ideals.

backbone: Reduce to finiteness of continuous stabilizer cohomology with mod-p coefficients, proved by downward induction over height strata using Fargues-Fontaine tower geometry and a highest-degree contradiction.
quote: We prove coefficient finiteness by downward induction from $A_n$.

backbone: Expand in exterior Faber polynomials, bound coefficient norms against boundary values, and use singular-vector pairing to obtain the constant-2 bound for matrix polynomials, then pass to arbitrary numerical ranges.
quote: Put $\gamma=\|F[A]\|$. There is nothing to prove if $\gamma=0$. Otherwise choose unit singular vectors $x,y\in\C^n\otimes\C^m$ such that

backbone: Confined isoperimetric minimizers exist; a sharp hypersurface Sobolev inequality applied to their boundaries gives a differential inequality for the profile whose integration is the model comparison.
quote: This gives one differential inequality whose integral is exactly the model comparison.

backbone: Induction on dimension; a least-area counterexample has index above m+3, so a deformed Lorentz-distance min-max family yields a smaller regular counterexample, a contradiction.
quote: Its mass is above the equator and below \(H\): it is a smaller counterexample, the desired contradiction.

backbone: Construct a warped metric on R^3 whose sphere links follow a periodic path cycling eigenlines through crossings, so selected harmonic modes average rates below k, exceeding the Euclidean count.
quote: We construct a periodic path $H(s)$ of sphere metrics near the round metric, all with the same pointwise area form.

backbone: Construct a smooth marginal whose optimal plans are forced by a supporting-potential certificate onto two triple families, with a mass imbalance making any deterministic Monge selection impossible.
quote: The construction has two parts: a geometric condition that forces every optimal plan onto two prescribed families of triples, and a mass imbalance that prevents a preserving map from choosing between them.
